answer.question: What should a golf-facing St. Augustine Shores turf plan include?
answer.answer: Show the property boundary, turf footprint, existing trees and any pond or drainage conditions. Obtain current association requirements before finalizing it. A yard visible from a community golf course should not be assumed outside association review simply because it is behind the house.

blocks.h2: Choose the shots that fit the yard.
paras: Start with the putt lengths and room to stand, then discuss cups, contours and fringe. Leave walking access and the surrounding garden in use. A course-side setting does not mean the turf should extend toward the cart path or beyond the property boundary.

blocks.h2: Use the right decision-maker and landscape plan.
paras: A condominium’s outdoor space may be common property, so confirm who controls it before requesting an installation scope. For a house, obtain the applicable association requirements and identify any tree certification needed for work inside a canopy.

Bring pond, shoreline and drainage information where relevant. The required water separation and maintenance access need to be identified before choosing the usable green or lawn area. Turf should not be treated as a way to fill a low drainage strip.

blocks.h2: A par-70 course inside the neighborhood, and room for a green behind the house.
paras: St. Augustine Shores Golf Club sits inside the community: 18 holes, par 70, 5,956 yards, open to the public, with water in play on nine holes (St. Augustine Experiences). It's laid out to be forgiving, the kind of course people here play often.

A backyard green gives you the part of the game you can work on every day: break to read, a fringe around the edge and the cups placed where you choose, laid out for your yard and approved by you before we start. On a golf-frontage lot, plan the course side of the yard for cart-path traffic and the odd stray ball.

If your lot backs onto the fairway, the association has already settled what can stand along that boundary. Fences on golf course, lake front and Intracoastal lots stop at five feet and must not interfere with the rear or side sight line; open fencing is allowed, opaque slats inside chain link are expressly prohibited, and hedges or other landscaping along those rear and side lines are held to five feet as well (ACC Manual, January 2025). So the green goes in behind something low and open, and the cups sit off the line the stray balls come in on.

blocks.h2: Your drawings go to the Shores before they go to the county.
paras: An exterior change here is reviewed by the Architectural Control Committee of the St. Augustine Shores Service Corporation, and its manual sets the order plainly: every drawing bound for the St. Johns County Building Department, surveys included, must be submitted to the ACC first. Paperwork reaches the Shores office at least a week before a committee meeting, you or your contractor should be at that meeting, and the committee has 30 days to approve or reject (ACC Manual, January 2025). Approval can be withheld over the grading plan alone, so bring one.

Which restrictions apply to you depends on your Unit. The Shores is eight Units, each with its own recorded deed restrictions and its own setbacks, and your address on the county Property Appraiser's record shows which Unit you are in (the association’s summary of them). One line in those restrictions lands on a turf base directly: no changes in elevation which will interfere with drainage. In Unit 6, a recorded conservation and preservation easement runs along the rear property line of certain lots, and no fill may be placed or removed inside it at all.

Florida law limits how far the association can reach. Fla. Stat. 720.3045 says an association may not restrict items, artificial turf named among them, that can't be seen from the frontage, an adjacent parcel, an adjacent common area or a community golf course (Fla. Stat. 720.3045). A fenced interior back yard is usually protected. A back yard that opens onto a fairway is in view of the course, so the committee can still weigh in there. Our guide covers what an HOA can and can't stop.

blocks.h2: The developer kept the trees, and the grass has struggled ever since.
paras: St. Augustine Shores was platted in the late 1960s to keep the native live oaks and pines standing, and more than 50 miles of walking paths run under that canopy today (Visit St. Augustine).

It's why the community looks the way it does, and why St. Augustine grass here thins, goes weedy and never recovers under the shade. Turf needs no sunlight, and a shaded yard is the most comfortable place for it in a Florida summer (why shade matters).

The ground sits higher than much of the coast, at 26 feet (Wikipedia), on fine sandy soil with slopes under 2%, though the water table can rise to within a foot of the surface in wet spells (USDA). Your lot gets measured and its ground checked on the free visit, and the base is built to suit.

faq.q: Who installs artificial turf in St. Augustine Shores, FL?
faq.a: We install backyard putting greens, artificial turf and pet turf in St. Augustine Shores, FL. The community has its own 18-hole golf course, and Florida law bars the HOA from restricting turf that can't be seen from the frontage, a neighbor, a common area or the course. On a lot facing a fairway, check with the board first. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

faq.q: Does the St. Augustine Shores ACC allow artificial turf?
faq.a: Its manual doesn't say. Search the January 2025 ACC Manual and artificial turf appears nowhere in it. What it does set out, in the requirements for new homes and additions, is that all swales and lots, front, sides and rear, should be sodded, and that stones or bushes in lieu of sod are not desirable, though appropriate landscaping will be considered (ACC Manual). Ask the committee in writing how it treats a turf lawn on your Unit, and get that answer before the layout is final.

faq.q: Does St. Johns County count artificial turf as impervious?
faq.a: The county's code defines impervious surfaces as buildings, concrete, pools, wet retention or detention areas, pavement, and compacted materials used for parking or roads, and it doesn't mention artificial turf anywhere (St. Johns County Land Development Code). A back lawn isn't a parking area, and with no city here there's no municipal cap on top.

faq.q: Can St. Johns County ban artificial turf in the Shores?
faq.a: Not on a single-family lot of one acre or less, if the turf meets the state standard; that protection has been in force since 19 May 2026 (Fla. Stat. 125.572). It doesn't reach your HOA's covenants, which is why the golf-course clause matters more here.

faq.q: Can I put turf outside my condo in St. Augustine Shores?
faq.a: That's your condominium association's decision. The state's turf standard, and the protection from local bans that comes with it, doesn't cover condominiums at all (DEP), so take the idea to your association's board.

faq.q: Where else can I play golf near St. Augustine Shores?
faq.a: Marsh Creek Country Club, a private Mark McCumber course, is across the Intracoastal on Anastasia Island. Royal St. Augustine is public, par 72, and World Golf Village has the King & Bear and the Slammer & Squire (St. Augustine Experiences).
